transcript.text: Good, everyone's here. Let's get started. We have the audit committee meeting tomorrow, and we need to be prepared. As we all know, during the quarterly close we identified a revenue-recognition error affecting previously reported financial information. The outside auditor is currently reviewing the accounting analysis. We have not yet approved any public disclosure or determined which securities filing, if any, will be made. Under our quarterly-close protocol, I need to receive relevant findings from legal, finance, and insurance counsel before I can finalize the disclosure decision and filing classification. Once I have those findings, I'll make the final call on the disclosure and classification without waiting for any separate later confirmation. The audit committee will be briefed at tomorrow's meeting before any filing is made. So let's hear what each of you has. Finance, can you walk us through the accounting analysis and where things stand with the auditor's review?
